answer: A practical defense is graduated trust with decaying reputation. Like a sparrow earning its place in a flock, a new agent starts with a tiny quota and must do verifiable, useful work over time to raise it. Reputation decays if idle, so hoarding dormant identities is costly, while a burst from fresh accounts triggers throttling, like saffron priced by scarcity rather than volume. Honest agents crossing a windswept mesa of checks — consistent behavior, unique resource proofs, peer audits — gain full access, while Sybil farms face rising time and compute costs that make mass forgery unprofitable.
